profile.name: Mina Cho
profile.household: Lives with both parents and a younger brother in a two-bedroom rental. Parents work in food service and a hospital laundry; Korean is spoken at home and English at school. She helps her brother with reading most evenings. A public bachelor's would require aid they have not yet figured out.
profile.school: Large public high school, grade 11. Literary magazine, one elective in another language, no shop classes this year. Library is reliable; home internet is shared and slow after dinner.
profile.wellbeing: No current concern stated. No classroom accommodations. She uses the school library when the apartment is noisy.
motivation: See whether more school is worth the cost
strengths: Revising wording after a reader reacts

Still learning to say when a task is no longer hers
profile.workContext: Quiet indoor table, unhurried revision, one partner or a small editorial group. No unusual physical access need.
constraints: Aid unclear for anything beyond local public college

profile.narrative: Mina revises bilingual short scenes for the literary magazine and rewrites an example when a classmate misses the tone. Six years of piano were her parents' priority; she almost never sits down at the keyboard now. Comparing wording still holds her, and she does not know whether a language-heavy bachelor's is feasible without substantial aid or whether she would rather keep writing than teach.
